source: Grossman & Boudaoud, Phys. Rev. Research 8, 013224 (2026), doi:10.1103/17sg-gzhl (CC BY 4.0) and its Supplemental Material. Values are transcribed from the text; nothing here is our own result.

foam_poisson_ratio.where: main text p. 6, Sec. II C 2 (Foamlike); Fig. 5
foam_poisson_ratio.construction: regular triangular lattice (phi = psi = 1, unit spacing), each vertex moved by a fixed distance eta in a uniformly random direction; the moved distances become the rest lengths (stress-free); all spring constants equal to 1
foam_poisson_ratio.simulation_protocol: strip 0 <= x <= 13, 0 <= y <= 52 (about 676 vertices), top and bottom rows held, top moved to y = 52 (1 + 0.01), energy minimised; width measured between the vertices initially closest to (0, 26) and (13, 26); nu = -delta / epsilon; 10 realizations (main text p. 9, Sec. V A)

honeycomb_poisson_ratio.geometry_as_we_read_it: hexagons with all six edges of unit length, distance 2 l between the two opposing vertices on the loading axis (l = 1 regular, l < 1/2 re-entrant); each hexagon triangulated with a centre vertex joined to the corners by springs of stiffness 1e-3 of the edges
honeycomb_poisson_ratio.claim: very high degree of agreement between Eq. (23) and the network calculation

ordered_lattice_poisson_ratio.where: Supplemental Material p. 2-3, Appendix C, Eq. (9); main text Fig. 4 and Eq. (25)
ordered_lattice_poisson_ratio.formula: nu = -P(phi, psi, Theta) / (4 Q(phi, psi, Theta)); P and Q as printed in Appendix C

triangular_lattice_moduli.where: Fig. 9 at eta = 0 (read from the vector data in paper_figures_vector.json)
triangular_lattice_moduli.note: unit spring constant and spacing; consistent with the exact values sqrt(3)/2 and sqrt(3)/4
